name: The Human Body & Health (AI-written, not yet reviewed)
description: 63 questions on the human body and staying healthy, from easy to hard (21 easy, 21 medium, 21 hard), written by Claude. Every question and answer needs checking by a person before anybody plays it.

source.name: Written by Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) on 2026-10-05, from its own knowledge plus the pages each item cites: no API call. Each item's `source` names the page its fact was confirmed on, or "common knowledge" with a reason where the fact is universal. Fact-check pending: no item carries `checked` yet, so a separate fact-check pass still has to go through every item, and a person still reviews it by playing.

review.how: Check every question, answer and explanation. Fix or delete what is wrong, set status to 'reviewed' with your name and the date, then move the file to packs/ and list it in pack_library.js.

items.question: What is the largest organ of the human body?
items.explain: Your skin covers and protects your whole body, making it your largest organ.

items.question: Which organ pumps blood around your body?
items.explain: Your heart's main job is moving blood all through your body.

items.question: Your heart is about the size of what?
items.explain: A heart is a fist-sized organ that works hard every moment.

items.question: How many chambers does the human heart have?
items.explain: The heart has two atria on top and two ventricles below.

items.question: Which organs do we use to breathe?
items.explain: Your lungs take in fresh air and let out the air you no longer need.

items.question: What is the colored part of your eye called?
items.explain: The iris gives your eyes their color and controls the size of the pupil.

items.question: What is the black circle in the middle of your eye called?
items.explain: The pupil is like a little window that lets light into your eye.

items.question: Where are most of your taste buds?
items.explain: Little bumps on your tongue hold thousands of taste buds.

items.question: Which is the longest bone in your body?
items.explain: The thigh bone, or femur, is the longest and strongest bone you have.

items.question: The smallest bones in your body are found in your...?
items.explain: Three tiny bones in each ear help carry sound.

items.question: How many permanent teeth do most adults have?
items.explain: Most grown-ups have 32 teeth, counting the wisdom teeth.

items.question: Which grow faster: fingernails or toenails?
answers: They grow at the same speed
items.explain: Fingernails grow about twice as fast as toenails.

items.question: How much sleep do most adults need each night?
items.explain: Seven to nine hours of sleep helps grown-ups feel their best.

items.question: Which vitamin is called the 'sunshine vitamin'?
items.explain: Your body makes vitamin D after spending time in the sun.

items.question: Oranges and other citrus fruits are well known for which vitamin?
items.explain: Citrus fruits are a tasty way to get vitamin C.

items.question: Your bones store which important mineral?
items.explain: Bones keep a supply of calcium that your body can use.

items.question: Which part of your blood carries oxygen around your body?
items.explain: Red blood cells deliver the oxygen your body needs for energy.

items.question: Where is a common place to check your own pulse?
items.explain: Just below the thumb side of your wrist you can feel your heartbeat.

items.question: Your kidneys are shaped like what?
items.explain: Kidneys look like big beans, each about the size of a fist.

items.question: The four main blood types are A, B, AB and which other?
items.explain: A, B, AB and O are the four main blood types.

items.question: Which part of your body do you smell with?
items.explain: Your nose detects scents and also warms and cleans the air you breathe.

items.question: What is the hardest substance in the human body?
items.explain: Tooth enamel is even harder than your bones.

items.question: How many baby teeth do most children have?
items.explain: Children usually have 20 baby teeth before their adult teeth come in.

items.question: What is the medical name for the kneecap?
items.explain: The patella sits at the front of your knee and helps your leg move.

items.question: About how many bones does an adult skeleton have?
items.explain: Most adults have between 206 and 213 bones.

items.question: Babies are usually born with about how many bones?
items.explain: Many of a baby's bones grow together into the adult skeleton.

items.question: The 'funny bone' in your elbow is not really a bone. What is it?
items.explain: That tingle comes from the ulnar nerve, not a bone at all.

items.question: Sweet, salty, sour and bitter are four basic tastes. What is the savory fifth one?
items.explain: Umami is the rich, savory taste in foods like tomatoes and mushrooms.

items.question: Fingernails are mostly made of which protein?
items.explain: Keratin keeps your nails strong.

items.question: What type of muscle is found only in the heart?
items.explain: Cardiac muscle exists nowhere else in your body.

items.question: Which is the biggest muscle in your body?
items.explain: The gluteus maximus in your seat helps you stand up, climb and run.

items.question: What connects your muscles to your bones?
items.explain: Tendons are strong cords that let muscles pull on bones.

items.question: What is the dome-shaped muscle under your lungs that helps you breathe?
items.explain: The diaphragm is your main breathing muscle.

items.question: What is the snail-shaped part of the inner ear that helps you hear?
items.explain: The fluid-filled cochlea turns sound vibrations into hearing.

items.question: Which cells in the eye let you see colors?
items.explain: Cones see color, while rods help you see in dim light.

items.question: Most dreams happen during which kind of sleep?
items.explain: REM stands for rapid eye movement, when most dreaming happens.

items.question: Adults are advised to get how many minutes of moderate activity, like brisk walking, each week?
items.explain: About 150 minutes a week of moderate activity keeps a body happy.

items.question: Which organ is famous for being able to regrow itself?
items.explain: The liver is one of the only organs that can regenerate itself.

items.question: Despite its name, which is the longest part of the digestive tract?
items.explain: It's called small because it is narrow, about as wide as a finger.

items.question: Where in your body is new blood made?
items.explain: Spongy marrow inside your bones makes your blood cells.

items.question: Which pigment determines the color of your skin, hair and eyes?
items.explain: How much melanin you have sets your skin, hair and eye color.

items.question: How many lobes does the right lung have?
items.explain: The right lung has three lobes and the left has two.

items.question: Which is the only bone in the human body that does not connect to another bone?
items.explain: The U-shaped hyoid in your throat is held in place only by muscles, ligaments and cartilage.

items.question: Which is the longest muscle in the human body?
items.explain: The long, thin sartorius runs from the hip across the thigh toward the knee.

items.question: What is the smallest bone in the human body?
items.explain: The stapes, or stirrup, in the middle ear is only a few millimeters across.

items.question: The incus, one of the tiny middle-ear bones, is nicknamed the...?
items.explain: The hammer, anvil and stirrup pass sound from the eardrum to the inner ear.

items.question: How many vertebrae are in the neck (cervical spine)?
items.explain: The neck has seven vertebrae, labeled C1 to C7.

items.question: The femur can support up to about how many times your body weight?
items.explain: Your thigh bone is remarkably strong for everyday walking and climbing.

items.question: What is the indent in the left lung that makes room for the heart called?
items.explain: The cardiac notch is why the left lung is a little smaller than the right.

items.question: What is the heart's natural pacemaker called?
items.explain: The SA node sends the signals that make your heart beat.

items.question: Laid end to end, about how many miles of blood vessels are in the human body?
items.explain: Your body has more than 60,000 miles of blood vessels.

items.question: Plasma, the liquid part of blood, makes up about what share of your blood?
items.explain: Plasma is about 55% of blood and red blood cells about 44%.

items.question: About how long does a red blood cell live?
items.explain: Red blood cells last about 120 days before the body makes fresh ones.

items.question: What is the first section of the small intestine called?
items.explain: The duodenum is a short chute of about 10 inches, followed by the jejunum and ileum.

items.question: What are the tiny filtering units inside the kidneys called?
items.explain: Each kidney has more than a million nephrons.

items.question: Which are the largest of the major salivary glands?
items.explain: The parotid glands, just in front of the ears, make about half your saliva.

items.question: Saliva contains which enzyme that starts breaking down starches?
items.explain: Amylase in saliva gets digestion going before food reaches the stomach.

items.question: What is the medical name for the eardrum?
items.explain: The tympanic membrane separates the outer ear from the middle ear.

items.question: Which tubes connect the middle ears to the throat and open when you yawn or swallow?
items.explain: Eustachian tubes even out the pressure inside your ears.

items.question: Which clear part of the eye has no blood vessels and takes in oxygen from the air through tears?
items.explain: Tears help the cornea absorb oxygen straight from the air.

items.question: What is the little half-moon shape at the base of a fingernail called?
items.explain: The lunula is easiest to see on your thumbnails.

items.question: Which layer of a tooth lies just underneath the enamel?
items.explain: Dentin sits under the enamel, with the soft pulp at the center.

items.question: About how many cells make up the human body?
items.explain: About 30 trillion cells work together to make you.
